page: Hetzner Cloud cpx12 is an entry-level virtual server based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing QEMU virtualization. It features a single shared vCPU from the AMD EPYC processor family running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 1 physical core and 1 thread. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 40 GB NVMe SSD, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included in the base configuration.

Benchmark results indicate a mixed performance profile. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2999.88. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core performance is weak, falling in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is generally constrained; the PassMark memory score and small-block read-only memory bandwidth of 146.65 GB/sec both rank in the bottom 10%, though large-block write bandwidth achieves an average rating at 28.87 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate average performance. Database and web serving capabilities are limited, with static web serving throughput at 2.11 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 2.79 million operations per second, both placing in the bottom 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the cpx12 instance is its shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity, which limits its suitability for multi-threaded or memory-intensive workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a highly accessible entry point for basic computing tasks, leveraging modern AMD EPYC hardware features such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography extensions without requiring dedicated resource pricing. This server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic utility scripting, low-traffic development environments, or simple background tasks that do not demand sustained multi-core processing or high memory bandwidth.
